In the temple
Among the poor

answers: The poor
The judges
The fatherless

answers: Defending the afflicted
Judging unjustly and accepting the persons of the wicked
Seeking justice from God

answers: To favor the wicked
To punish the wicked
To remove the wicked from court

The judges are under God's observation and authority
God has canceled the judgment

The judges do not have to give an account
The judges are measured by a higher moral standard

answers: God is present in judgment, while the judges are practicing injustice
The poor are contrasted only with the rich
The earth is contrasted with the nations

challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 1–2?

To rebuke a continuing condition of injustice
To announce that judgment has ended

short_answers.question: According to verse 1, who judges among the gods?

paragraphs.title: The Duty to Protect the Helpless

answers: The wicked
The poor and fatherless
The judges alone
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Defend the poor and fatherless.”
easy.q: Whom are the judges commanded to defend?

answers: The poor and needy
The princes
The nations
easy.explanation: Verse 4 commands, “Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.”
easy.q: Whom should the judges deliver from the hand of the wicked?

answers: Society becomes stronger
Everyone is delivered
The foundations of the earth are out of course
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says that all the foundations of the earth are out of course.
easy.q: What happens when the judges do not know or understand?

answers: Both express a duty to protect the vulnerable in court and in practice
The first concerns the wicked, while the second concerns the judges
They have no connection
medium.explanation: The verses require both fair judgment and practical rescue for helpless people.
medium.q: What is the connection between doing justice to the afflicted and delivering the poor and needy?

answers: All the temples
The foundations of society and order
All the roads of the earth
medium.explanation: The expression points to the basic structures that support society and justice.
medium.q: What does “all the foundations of the earth” mean in this context?

answers: Because the poor receive too much protection
Because the judges fail to understand and act justly
Because there are too many nations
medium.explanation: The judges walk in darkness and fail to fulfill their responsibility, disturbing society's foundations.
medium.q: According to these verses, why are the foundations of society shaken?

answers: Justice exists only for the powerful
Justice includes active responsibility toward the weak
Justice means avoiding all intervention
challenge.explanation: The judges must defend, do justice, deliver, and rescue the helpless.
challenge.q: What view of justice is presented in verses 3–4?

answers: Treatment of the weak affects society as a whole
The poor are not part of society
The judgment concerns only one particular land
challenge.explanation: The passage connects injustice toward individuals with disorder throughout society.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from protecting individuals to the foundations of the earth?

answers: Defend the vulnerable, deliver them from the wicked, then describe the results of failure
Describe the judges' fall, appoint them, and then protect the fatherless
Deliver the wicked, judge the poor, and then praise the judges
challenge.explanation: The passage first gives commands for justice and then describes the darkness and disorder caused by failure.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the message of verses 3–5?

As wicked men
As poor and needy people

The poor

All nations
